small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_SP (e.g., 256) paired with BLOCK_OC=64/128 to better amortize the weight tile reload across 4 pooled-position accumulators; also try BLOCK_K=128 with num_stages=2 since K_TOTAL=576 divides evenly.
- Swap the program-id ordering so pid_sp is axis 0 (or use program_id swizzling) to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across batch — currently pid_n=axis0 launches 128 batches sequentially per (oc,sp) and reloads weights each time.
- Try storing the output in NHWC layout (or at least writing with sp-contiguous stores already done) and consider preloading bias once outside the K loop (already done) — also experiment with num_stages=4 on the BLOCK_K=32 configs.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM where the K dimension iterates only IC (with KH*KW=9 fully unrolled inside): load a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] weight slab once and reuse it across all 9 kernel positions × 4 pooled sub-positions, dramatically increasing arithmetic intensity per weight load.
- Switch to a persistent-CTA design that tiles (OC, spatial) and loops over N inside the kernel, so the weight tile is loaded once from HBM and reused across the entire batch (weights are 64*128*9*4B = 288KB, tiles are tiny and very reusable).
- Use channels-last input layout (NHWC) and load IC as the contiguous GEMM-K axis with vectorized 128-bit loads; this makes the input gather coalesced and lets each pooled output naturally consume a 2×2 contiguous block.
